commands.name: agent-reach
commands.description:
MUST USE when user wants to 调研/research/搜索/search/查/找/look up anything on the internet — e.g. 全网调研 X / 帮我调研一下 X / 查一下 X / 搜搜 X / 看看大家怎么评价 X / X 上有什么讨论 / research this topic。
Also MUST USE when user mentions any platform or shares any URL/链接: 小红书/xiaohongshu/xhs, Twitter/推特/X, B站/bilibili, Reddit, Facebook, Instagram, V2EX, LinkedIn/领英/招聘/求职/jobs, YouTube, GitHub code search, 小宇宙播客, 雪球/股票行情, RSS feeds, or any web URL.
15 platforms, multi-backend routing (OpenCLI / per-platform CLIs / APIs). Zero config for 6 channels. Run `agent-reach doctor --json` to see which backend serves each platform right now.
NOT for: 写报告/数据分析/翻译等内容加工（本 skill 只负责从互联网获取内容）； 发帖/评论/点赞等写操作；已有专门 skill 的平台（先用专门 skill）。
【路由方式】SKILL.md 包含路由表和常用命令，复杂场景需按需阅读对应分类的 references/*.md。 分类：search / social (小红书/推特/B站/V2EX/Reddit/Facebook/Instagram) / career(LinkedIn) / dev(github) / web(网页/文章/RSS) / video(YouTube/B站/播客)。 (user)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation. (user)

commands.name: mcp-builder
commands.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK). (user)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (user)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions. (user)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (user)

commands.name: ui-ux-pro-max
commands.description: UI/UX design intelligence for web and mobile. Searchable local database with 84 styles, 192 color palettes, 74 font pairings, 192 product types, 98 UX guidelines, 104 icon entries, 16 GSAP motion presets, and 25 chart types across 22 stacks (React, Next.js, Vue, Nuxt, Svelte, Astro, SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Jetpack Compose, Angular, Laravel, JavaFX, WPF, WinUI, Avalonia, Uno Platform, UWP, Three.js, and HTML/CSS). Use when designing, building, or reviewing UI: pages, components, color schemes, typography, layout, accessibility, animation, or data visualization. (user)

commands.name: web-artifacts-builder
commands.description: Suite of tools for creating elaborate, multi-component claude.ai HTML artifacts using modern frontend web technologies (React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui). Use for complex artifacts requiring state management, routing, or shadcn/ui components - not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts. (user)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (user)

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.description: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.

commands.name: artifact-diagramming
commands.description: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

168	now(){ date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

171	# Best-effort on purpose: logging must never turn a decision into a crash.
172	logrow(){ # <task_id> <depth> <decision> <detail>
173	  # Best-effort log append; when the routing store is unwritable the row goes

178	    { printf 'routing-gate UNLOGGED(store unwritable): %s %s %s %s\n' "${1:--}" "${2:--}" "${3:--}" "${4:--}" >&9; } 2>/dev/null || printf 'routing-gate UNLOGGED(store unwritable): %s %s %s %s\n' "${1:--}" "${2:--}" "${3:--}" "${4:--}" >&2 || true

182	# The ONE label block, shared verbatim with record-degradation.sh (the suite
183	# diffs the two writers' label blocks so they cannot drift apart). EXACT vs
184	# ESTIMATE is labeled per field — the operator's rule, in the artefact itself.
185	write_labels(){ # <dest-file> <receipt-basename> — create-once via noclobber
186	  ( set -C; { \
187	    printf '# live state for %s — append-only; counts are DERIVED by counting rows, never stored\n' "$2"; \
188	    printf 'label\ttask_dispatches\tEXACT (hook-counted ALLOW decisions at PreToolUse, in sessions where the gate is loaded; attempts, not completions)\n'; \

191	    printf 'label\ttool_failures\tEXACT only where PostToolUse exposes success:false/is_error; otherwise unavailable — absence of a row is NOT evidence of success\n'; \

214	# The open receipt: among build-os/packets/routing/*.md with executed_mode '-',
215	# the newest by the trailing UTC stamp in the file name (route-task.sh's own
216	# naming), falling back to mtime order for foreign names.
217	open_receipt(){
218	  local f best="" bestkey=""
219	  [ -d "$RDIR" ] || return 1
220	  while IFS= read -r f; do
221	    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
222	    [ "$(fval "$f" executed_mode)" = "-" ] || continue

238	# Prints a decision protocol on stdout: first line ALLOW or BLOCK, message
239	# after. The wrapper turns BLOCK into exit 2 + stderr; anything malformed —
240	# including this function crashing — FAILS OPEN.
241	gate_decide(){ # <stdin-json>
242	  local in="$1" sub rec mode esc esc_ev deg bud allow ntask nproc kind
243	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
244	  sub="$(printf '%s' "$in" | jq -r '.tool_input.subagent_type // "-"' 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
245	  [ -n "$sub" ] || sub="-"
246	  rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
247	  if [ -z "$rec" ]; then
248	    logrow "none" "-" "BLOCK-NO-RECEIPT" "subagent_type=$sub"
249	    printf 'BLOCK\n'
250	    printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — no OPEN routing receipt exists under build-os/packets/routing/ (open = executed_mode "-"). A substantive task cannot execute unrouted: issue a routing receipt first via build-os/tools/route-task.sh --task-id <id> --description <text> --descriptor <13-field-json>, then dispatch again. Continue the task — only this unrouted dispatch is refused, not the work.\n'
251	    return 0
252	  fi
253	  mode="$(fval "$rec" selected_mode)"
254	  esc="$(fval "$rec" escalation)"; esc_ev="$(fval "$rec" escalation_evidence)"
255	  deg="$(fval "$rec" degradation_note)"
256	  local task_id; task_id="$(fval "$rec" task_id)"; [ -n "$task_id" ] || task_id="-"
257	
258	  # Dispatch class: process roles are governance ceremony, counted against the
259	  # allowance and attributed governance_process; everything else is task work.
260	  kind="task"
261	  local r; for r in $PROCESS_ROLES; do [ "$sub" = "$r" ] && kind="process"; done
262	
263	  # Effective depth: a filled degradation_note means the receipt has already
264	  # been downgraded to gravito_light — the degradation is binding. An
265	  # evidence-bearing escalation record lifts direct/light to full (escalation
266	  # is legal; silence is not — evidence required, exactly as routing-check.sh).
267	  local eff="$mode" escalated=0
268	  if [ -n "$deg" ] && [ "$deg" != "-" ]; then
269	    eff="gravito_light_degraded"
270	  elif [ "$mode" != "gravito_full" ] && [ "$esc" != "-" ] && [ -n "$esc" ] && [ "$esc_ev" != "-" ] && [ -n "$esc_ev" ]; then
271	    eff="gravito_full"; escalated=1
272	  fi
273	
274	  case "$eff" in
275	    gravito_full) : ;;
276	    gravito_light_degraded)
277	      logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "BLOCK-DEGRADED" "subagent_type=$sub"
278	      printf 'BLOCK\n'
279	      printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — receipt %s is DEGRADED to gravito_light (degradation_note is filled), so new dispatch is ceremony above the degraded depth. 280	      return 0 ;;
281	    direct|gravito_light)
282	      logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "BLOCK-MODE-$mode" "subagent_type=$sub"
283	      printf 'BLOCK\n'
284	      printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — the open routing receipt %s records %s, and subagent dispatch is ceremony above that depth: executing above the recorded mode with no evidence-bearing escalation record is silent escalation (the executed T5 defect), refused here BEFORE execution rather than at close. Either continue the task in the parent loop at %s, or record a new evidence-bearing escalation decision in the receipt (fill escalation AND escalation_evidence, naming what changed) and dispatch again. Continue the task — only the dispatch is refused, not the work.\n' "$(basename "$rec")" "$mode" "$mode"
285	      return 0 ;;
286	    *) return 1 ;;  # unreadable mode -> fail open in the wrapper
287	  esac
288	
289	  if [ "$kind" = "process" ]; then
290	    allow="$(fval "$rec" process_dispatch_allowance)"
291	    is_num "$allow" || allow="$DEFAULT_PROCESS_ALLOWANCE"
292	    nproc="$(count_kind "$rec" process_dispatch)"
293	    if [ "$nproc" -ge "$allow" ]; then
294	      logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "BLOCK-PROCESS-ALLOWANCE" "subagent_type=$sub n=$nproc allowance=$allow"
295	      printf 'BLOCK\n'
296	      printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — process-role dispatches are at the allowance (%s of %s, receipt %s; this dispatch is subagent_type %s, attributed governance_process). The gate chain is governance ceremony with its own budget, separate from task work. Consolidate remaining gate work into the parent loop, preserve completed outputs, and continue the task. Stop the expensive mode, not the task — do not stop working.\n' "$nproc" "$allow" "$(basename "$rec")" "$sub"
297	      return 0
298	    fi
299	    staterow "$rec" process_dispatch "subagent_type=$sub attributed=governance_process" || return 1
300	    logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "ALLOW-PROCESS-DISPATCH" "subagent_type=$sub n=$((nproc+1)) allowance=$allow"
301	    printf 'ALLOW\n'
302	    return 0
303	  fi
304	
305	  # Task dispatch against budget_max_subagents. An escalated receipt carries
306	  # its pre-escalation budget (0 for direct/light), so the Full derived default
307	  # (3) governs where the recorded budget is below it — otherwise an escalation
308	  # would be granted and immediately unusable.
309	  bud="$(fval "$rec" budget_max_subagents)"
310	  is_num "$bud" || bud=0
311	  if [ "$escalated" = "1" ] && [ "$bud" -lt 3 ]; then bud=3; fi
312	  ntask="$(count_kind "$rec" task_dispatch)"
313	  if [ "$ntask" -ge "$bud" ]; then
314	    # THE LIVE BRAKE — before close, not at it. Fire-once degradation: stamp
315	    # via record-degradation.sh (which also appends the DEGRADATION state row).
316	    if [ "$deg" = "-" ] && [ -x "$RECDEG" ]; then
317	      bash "$RECDEG" --receipt "$rec" \
318	        --reason "fan-out throttle: task dispatches at budget_max_subagents ($ntask of $bud); stopped spawning" \
319	        --evidence "live state $SDIR/$(basename "$rec" .md).tsv ($ntask completed dispatch rows preserved)" \
320	        >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
321	    fi
322	    logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "BLOCK-FANOUT-BUDGET" "subagent_type=$sub n=$ntask budget=$bud degradation=stamped"
323	    printf 'BLOCK\n'
324	    printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — task dispatches are at budget_max_subagents (%s of %s, receipt %s). The degradation has been recorded on the receipt, so an honest close passes the budget gate. Stop the expensive mode, not the task — do not stop working.\n' "$ntask" "$bud" "$(basename "$rec")"
325	    return 0
326	  fi
327	  staterow "$rec" task_dispatch "subagent_type=$sub attributed=task_execution" || return 1
328	  # Close-fill tooling for the contribution table: one stub row per admitted
329	  # Full task dispatch, all '-' (admissions to be filled at close, never zeros).
330	  printf 'contribution: %s | - | - | changed_implementation=- | changed_conclusion=- | caught_defect=- | duplicated_work=- | tokens=- | cost=- | time=-\n' "$sub" >> "$rec" 2>/dev/null || true
331	  logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "ALLOW-TASK-DISPATCH" "subagent_type=$sub n=$((ntask+1)) budget=$bud"

333	  return 0

336	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- count ------
337	# The always-on observer. Never blocks, never parses with jq (a node/jq spawn
338	# per tool call is exactly the overhead this path must not carry): one sed pull
339	# of tool_name, one grep per receipt to find the open one, one append.
340	# PACKET-0054: chars= is the ESTIMATE token-proxy input (length of everything
341	# after "tool_input" in the raw event — a chars proxy, not a parse); Read/Grep/
342	# Glob get an exploratory_event row beside their tool_event row; and arm_check
343	# arms the repetitive-loop trip the mutgate enforces.
344	count_tool(){ # <stdin-json>
345	  local in="$1" tool rec ti chars
346	  tool="$(printf '%s' "$in" | sed -n 's/.*"tool_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
347	  [ -n "$tool" ] || tool="-"
348	  rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
349	  [ -n "$rec" ] || return 0   # no open receipt: nothing to count against, no state invented
350	  ti="${in#*\"tool_input\"}"; chars="${#ti}"
351	  staterow "$rec" tool_event "tool_name=$tool chars=$chars" || return 1
352	  case "$tool" in
353	    Read|Grep|Glob) staterow "$rec" exploratory_event "tool_name=$tool source=read_class" || return 1 ;;
354	  esac
355	  arm_check "$rec" || return 1
356	  return 0

359	# Arm the reassessment trip when the window since the last boundary row
360	# (reassess_block / reassess_reset) shows a repetitive parent loop. Arming is
361	# once per window; the trip itself fires ONCE, at the next mutation-capable
362	# call (mutgate). Counters are DERIVED by reading rows, never stored.
363	arm_check(){ # <receipt-path>
364	  local sf run sum armed trip="" val="" thr="" tier="" bud esc_s deg_s v
365	  sf="$SDIR/$(basename "$1" .md).tsv"
366	  [ -f "$sf" ] || return 0
367	  read -r run sum armed <<EOF
368	$(awk -F'\t' '
369	    $2=="reassess_block"||$2=="reassess_reset"{run=0;sum=0;last="";armed=0;next}
370	    $2=="reassess_armed"{armed=1;next}
371	    $2=="tool_event"{
372	      t=""; if(match($3,/tool_name=[^ ]*/)) t=substr($3,RSTART+10,RLENGTH-10);
373	      if(t!="" && t==last) run++; else {run=1;last=t};
374	      if(match($3,/chars=[0-9]+/)) sum+=substr($3,RSTART+6,RLENGTH-6)+0 }
375	    END{print run+0, sum+0, armed+0}' "$sf")
376	EOF
377	  [ "$armed" = "1" ] && return 0
378	  if [ "$run" -ge "$SAME_TOOL_MAX" ] 2>/dev/null; then
379	    trip="same_tool"; val="$run"; thr="$SAME_TOOL_MAX"; tier="EXACT"
380	  else
381	    bud="$(fval "$1" budget_max_uncached_tokens)"
382	    if is_num "$bud" && [ "$((sum / 4))" -ge "$((PROXY_MULT * bud))" ]; then
383	      trip="proxy"; val="$((sum / 4))"; thr="$((PROXY_MULT * bud))"; tier="ESTIMATE"
384	    fi
385	  fi
386	  [ -n "$trip" ] || return 0
387	  esc_s="-"; deg_s="-"
388	  v="$(fval "$1" escalation_evidence)"; [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != "-" ] && esc_s="set"
389	  v="$(fval "$1" degradation_note)";    [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != "-" ] && deg_s="set"
390	  staterow "$1" reassess_armed "trip=$trip value=$val threshold=$thr tier=$tier esc=$esc_s deg=$deg_s" || return 1
391	  return 0
392	}

395	# The UNIVERSAL TASK-ENTRY boundary (PACKET-0054): every mutation-capable tool
396	# call requires an open routing receipt — including parent-only work that never
397	# dispatches. Classification is a NAMED HEURISTIC (stated in
398	# routing_contract_live.md): a hostile command evades the mutation class with
399	# sh -c or a wrapper; this gate is discipline-for-honest-agents plus an audit
400	# trail, NOT a sandbox — the sandbox is the platform's permission system.
401	#
402	# THE STRUCTURED ROUTING ACTION (PACKET-0055). The deadlock-guard exception —
403	# the SOLE ungated pass in the task-entry boundary — no longer substring-
404	# matches the raw event (the operator ruled that breadth "a real enforcement
405	# bypass, not merely a wording issue"). It fires only when the ACTUAL
406	# tool_input.command field, extracted and trimmed, IS exactly one clean
407	# routing-tool invocation: an optional interpreter prefix (bash/sh for the .sh
408	# tools, node for mode-select.mjs), an optional path prefix, exactly one of
409	# route-task.sh | mode-select.mjs | routing-check.sh | record-degradation.sh,
410	# then arguments free of every chaining/substitution metacharacter — no ';',
411	# '&', '|', backtick, '$(', '<', '>', no newline; quotes, braces, brackets,
412	# colons and commas stay legal, so the refusal's own quoted-JSON --descriptor
413	# recovery example passes. Everything that merely MENTIONS a routing tool —
414	# compound commands, comments, sh -c/eval wrappers, substitution, routing-tool
415	# paths in non-command fields — and every event the extractor cannot read
416	# falls THROUGH to normal classification: extraction fails TOWARD GATING,
417	# never toward an ungated pass (the recovery command is clean and always
418	# extracts, so the fall-through cannot re-create the deadlock). The extraction
419	# is itself a heuristic over JSON-in-shell, and that failure direction is its
420	# stated bound.
421	RT_STRICT='^((bash|sh) +)?([A-Za-z0-9._/-]*/)?(route-task\.sh|routing-check\.sh|record-degradation\.sh)( |$)|^(node +)?([A-Za-z0-9._/-]*/)?mode-select\.mjs( |$)'
422	
423	extract_command(){ # <raw-json> -> tool_input.command's JSON string content (escape-encoded); rc 1 = absent/unreadable
424	  local in="$1" rest raw
425	  case "$in" in *'"command"'*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
426	  # First occurrence of the unescaped key: a decoy INSIDE a JSON string value
427	  # is necessarily \"-escaped, so its colon-quote shape cannot match below.
428	  rest="${in#*\"command\"}"
429	  raw="$(printf '%s' "$rest" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\(\([^"\\]\|\\.\)*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
430	  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 1
431	  printf '%s' "$raw"
432	}
433	
434	routing_action(){ # <raw-json> -> "<tool>\t<decoded command>" iff the command IS one clean routing invocation; rc 1 otherwise
435	  local in="$1" raw cmd stripped t BS='\' SENT=$'\x01'
436	  raw="$(extract_command "$in")" || return 1
437	  # Only the benign JSON escapes \" \\ \/ may appear: any other escape (\n,
438	  # \t, \u003b, ...) could conceal a metacharacter from the checks below, so
439	  # its presence falls through — toward gating.
440	  stripped="$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed 's|\\["\\/]||g')"
441	  case "$stripped" in *"$BS"*) return 1 ;; esac
442	  # Decode the three benign escapes so the checks and the fingerprint see the
443	  # command exactly as the shell receives it. Decoding cannot conceal a
444	  # forbidden character: none of the three decodes to one.
445	  cmd=${raw//"$BS$BS"/$SENT}
446	  cmd=${cmd//"$BS"\"/\"}
447	  cmd=${cmd//"$BS"\//\/}
448	  cmd=${cmd//$SENT/$BS}
449	  cmd="${cmd#"${cmd%%[! ]*}"}"; cmd="${cmd%"${cmd##*[! ]}"}"
450	  [ -n "$cmd" ] || return 1
451	  case "$cmd" in
452	    *';'*|*'&'*|*'|'*|*'`'*|*'$('*|*'<'*|*'>'*|*$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*$'\r'*) return 1 ;;
453	  esac
454	  printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -qE "$RT_STRICT" || return 1
455	  t="$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -oE 'route-task\.sh|mode-select\.mjs|routing-check\.sh|record-degradation\.sh' | head -n1)"
456	  printf '%s\t%s' "$t" "$cmd"
457	}

468	#
469	# EXP-0005 measured every Gravito arm producing zero mutations. Reproduction
470	# refuted the recorded cause: the gate ALLOWS route-task.sh and route-task.sh
471	# works on a clean clone. What failed was one layer out — the HOST permission
472	# layer refused the Bash invocation in headless sessions with no approver.
473	#
474	# The defect is a PERMISSION-CLASS MISMATCH: earning first authority required
475	# Bash (frequently approval-gated) even when the authorized work needed only
476	# Edit/Write (auto-approved). Native paid host denials as friction because its
477	# work path was Edit; Gravito paid one as total paralysis because Edit itself
478	# was gated behind that Bash call.
479	#
480	# THE INVARIANT: first mutation authority must not depend on an operation class
481	# whose host permission requirements are stricter than the mutation class it
482	# authorizes.
483	#
484	# THE CHANNEL: a routing request may be expressed by WRITING one file. Writes
485	# to that exact path — and no other — are ungated, because the path is the
486	# routing channel, not product mutation. Writing it authorizes NOTHING by
487	# itself: the request is schema-checked and then routed through the ordinary
488	# route-task.sh, so the descriptor, the mode selection and every downstream
489	# budget/escalation/close rule apply unchanged.
490	REQ_FILE="$RDIR/routing-request.json"

492	extract_file_path(){ # <raw-json> -> tool_input.file_path; rc 1 = absent
493	  local in="$1" rest raw
494	  case "$in" in *'"file_path"'*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
495	  rest="${in#*\"file_path\"}"
496	  raw="$(printf '%s' "$rest" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\(\([^"\\]\|\\.\)*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
497	  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 1
498	  printf '%s' "$raw"

502	  local fp; fp="$(extract_file_path "$1")" || return 1

509	mut_classify(){ # <raw-json> <tool> -> routing_tool | git_readonly | mutation | other
510	  local in="$1" tool="$2"
511	  case "$tool" in
512	    Edit|Write|NotebookEdit)
513	      # The routing channel itself is not product mutation. Exactly one path.
514	      if is_routing_request_path "$in"; then printf 'routing_request'; return 0; fi
515	      printf 'mutation'; return 0 ;;
516	    Bash) : ;;
517	    *) printf 'other'; return 0 ;;
518	  esac
519	  # DEADLOCK GUARD, structured (PACKET-0055): exactly-recognized routing
520	  # invocations only — without an ungated pass here no session could issue the
521	  # receipt its first gated call requires; anything short of an exact
522	  # invocation falls through to the git/mutation classes and gates.
523	  if routing_action "$in" >/dev/null; then printf 'routing_tool'; return 0; fi
524	  if printf '%s' "$in" | grep -qE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])git([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)'; then
525	    # Any git command carrying a mutating subcommand or a force flag is
526	    # mutation-capable — checked FIRST so `git status && git push` gates.
527	    if printf '%s' "$in" | grep -qE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])(push|commit|merge|rebase|reset|checkout|restore|clean|apply|am|cherry-pick|tag|stash)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)|--force(-with-lease)?([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)|[[:space:]]-f([[:space:]\"\\]|$)'; then
528	      printf 'mutation'; return 0
529	    fi
530	    # The read-only inspection class, by git subcommand. `git -C dir status`
531	    # and other indirections fall through to mutation-capable — conservative.
532	    if printf '%s' "$in" | grep -qE 'git[[:space:]]+(status|log|diff|show|rev-parse|ls-files|branch)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)'; then
533	      printf 'git_readonly'; return 0
534	    fi
535	    printf 'mutation'; return 0
536	  fi
537	  printf 'mutation'   # Bash defaults to mutation-capable: the boundary is entry, not tool trivia
538	}

540	# Route a pending request through the ordinary tool. Returns 0 only when a
541	# receipt was actually minted. Deterministic, idempotent (the request is
542	# consumed), and audited with the request's sha256.
543	redeem_routing_request(){
544	  [ -f "$REQ_FILE" ] || return 1
545	  command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || { logrow "none" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-REQUEST-REFUSED" "reason=node-unavailable"; return 1; }
546	
547	  local tid desc descr sha rt out
548	  # Schema check: task_id, description and a descriptor object must all be
549	  # present. Anything missing is a refusal, never a permissive default.
550	  if ! node -e '
551	    const fs=require("fs");
552	    const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8"));
553	    if(!j.task_id||!j.description||!j.descriptor||typeof j.descriptor!=="object") process.exit(1);
554	    if(!/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$/.test(j.task_id)) process.exit(1);
555	  ' "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
556	    sha="$(sha256sum "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-12)"
557	    logrow "none" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-REQUEST-REFUSED" "reason=schema-invalid sha256=${sha:--}"
558	    rm -f "$REQ_FILE"
559	    return 1
560	  fi
561	
562	  tid="$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8")).task_id)' "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
563	  desc="$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8")).description)' "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
564	  descr="$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8")).descriptor))' "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
565	  sha="$(sha256sum "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-12)"
566	  rt="$DATA_ROOT/build-os/tools/route-task.sh"
567	  [ -x "$rt" ] || [ -f "$rt" ] || { logrow "none" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-REQUEST-REFUSED" "reason=route-task-missing"; return 1; }
568	
569	  # Consume FIRST, so a failing route cannot be retried in a loop.
570	  rm -f "$REQ_FILE"
571	  out="$(bash "$rt" --task-id "$tid" --description "$desc" --descriptor "$descr" 2>&1)" || {
572	    logrow "none" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-REQUEST-REFUSED" "reason=route-task-failed sha256=${sha:--} detail=$(printf '%s' "$out" | tr -d '\t\r\n' | cut -c1-120)"
573	    return 1
574	  }
575	  logrow "$tid" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-RECEIPT-MINTED" "via=routing-request-channel sha256=${sha:--} task_id=$tid"
576	  return 0
577	}

579	mutgate_decide(){ # <stdin-json> — protocol on stdout: ALLOW or BLOCK + message
580	  local in="$1" tool cls rec tid="none" mode="-" v act rtool rcmd sha exc
581	  tool="$(printf '%s' "$in" | sed -n 's/.*"tool_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
582	  [ -n "$tool" ] || return 1   # unreadable event -> fail open in the wrapper
583	  cls="$(mut_classify "$in" "$tool")"
584	  rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
585	  if [ -n "$rec" ]; then tid="$(fval "$rec" task_id)"; mode="$(fval "$rec" selected_mode)"; [ -n "$tid" ] || tid="-"; fi
586	  case "$cls" in
587	    routing_tool)
588	      # THE ACTION FINGERPRINT (PACKET-0055): the pass row records WHICH tool
589	      # matched, the first 12 hex chars of the exact command's sha256, and a
590	      # sanitized <=80-char excerpt (tabs/newlines stripped — the ledgers are
591	      # TSV). Only exact invocations reach this label at all, so the ledger
592	      # alone now distinguishes "ran route-task.sh" from anything else.
593	      act="$(routing_action "$in")" || act=$'-\t-'
594	      rtool="${act%%$'\t'*}"; rcmd="${act#*$'\t'}"
595	      sha="-"
596	      if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
597	        sha="$(printf '%s' "$rcmd" | sha256sum 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-12)"; [ -n "$sha" ] || sha="-"
598	      fi
599	      exc="$(printf '%s' "$rcmd" | tr -d '\t\r\n' | cut -c1-80)"
600	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "ROUTING-TOOL-PASS" "tool=$tool ungated=deadlock-guard routing_tool=$rtool sha256=$sha cmd=$exc"
601	      [ -n "$rec" ] && { staterow "$rec" routing_tool_pass "tool_name=$tool routing_tool=$rtool sha256=$sha cmd=$exc" || true; }
602	      printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0 ;;
603	    git_readonly)
604	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "GIT-READONLY-PASS" "tool=$tool class=exploratory heuristic=git-subcommand"
605	      [ -n "$rec" ] && { staterow "$rec" exploratory_event "tool_name=$tool source=git_readonly" || true; }
606	      printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0 ;;
607	    routing_request)
608	      # Writing the request authorizes NOTHING. It is allowed because the path
609	      # is the routing channel, and it is logged so the ledger shows the
610	      # request separately from the receipt it may later mint.
611	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "ROUTING-REQUEST-WRITE" "tool=$tool ungated=bootstrap-channel path=routing-request.json"
612	      printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0 ;;
613	    other)
614	      printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0 ;;
615	  esac
616	  if [ -z "$rec" ]; then
617	    # BOOTSTRAP REDEMPTION. A pending, schema-valid request is routed through
618	    # the ordinary route-task.sh — from inside the hook, which executes outside
619	    # the tool-permission layer. That is the whole fix: the worker earned
620	    # authority using the SAME permission class as the work it authorizes.
621	    # A malformed request mints nothing and the block below stands.
622	    if redeem_routing_request; then
623	      rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
624	      if [ -n "$rec" ]; then
625	        tid="$(fval "$rec" task_id)"; mode="$(fval "$rec" selected_mode)"
626	        printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0
627	      fi
628	    fi
629	  fi
630	  if [ -z "$rec" ]; then
631	    if ! store_available; then
632	      # STORE-UNAVAILABLE IS NOT A BRICK (PACKET-0055): with the store neither
633	      # readable nor creatable, route-task.sh could never write the receipt a
634	      # block would demand — a refusal here is a dead end whose own recovery
635	      # command cannot succeed. FAIL OPEN instead, traced: the row itself
636	      # rides the stderr fallback (UNLOGGED(store unwritable)) whenever the
637	      # log file shares the store's fate — the layer-4 mechanics of 0053.
638	      logrow "none" "-" "FAIL-OPEN-STORE-UNAVAILABLE" "tool=$tool store unreadable and uncreatable: recovery cannot succeed, so blocking would be a dead end"
639	      printf 'ALLOW\n'
640	      return 0
641	    fi
642	    logrow "none" "-" "BLOCK-MUTATION-NO-RECEIPT" "tool=$tool"
643	    printf 'BLOCK\n'
644	    # THE REFUSAL IS GENERATED BY THE SELECTOR, not hand-authored here. One
645	    # ruleset decides both what self-audit calls incompatible and what the
646	    # worker is told to do, so the advertised recovery cannot drift away from
647	    # the path that actually works on this host. A static message that says
648	    # "run this Bash command" while the host denies Bash is how EXP-0005
649	    # produced 0/12.
650	    # CODE_ROOT, not DATA_ROOT. The recovery generator is CODE that ships with
651	    # this gate, not per-repo DATA. Resolving it under the data root meant that
652	    # whenever the two differ -- which is the entire purpose of
653	    # ROUTING_GATE_ROOT / CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR -- the selector silently could not
654	    # be found, and the gate fell through to the fallback that advertises the
655	    # shell route unconditionally. That is precisely the behaviour the selector
656	    # was made load-bearing to prevent, reappearing in the one configuration
657	    # nobody ran. The same call already resolves --gate under CODE_ROOT.
658	    _rec="$CODE_ROOT/build-os/assumptions/gate-recovery.mjs"
659	    if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$_rec" ] \
660	       && node "$_rec" --tool "$tool" --gate "$CODE_ROOT/.claude/hooks/routing-gate.sh" 2>/dev/null; then
661	      logrow "$tid" "-" "RECOVERY-SELECTED" "tool=$tool host=${GRAVITO_HOST_PROFILE:-unknown_conservative} source=selector"
662	    else
663	      # Fail toward DISCOVERABILITY: with no selector, advertise every route
664	      # rather than none, lowest privilege first. A worker told nothing cannot
665	      # proceed; a worker told too much merely spends one extra call.
666	      printf 'routing-gate: MUTATION BLOCKED — %s is mutation-capable and NO OPEN routing receipt exists under build-os/packets/routing/.\n' "$tool"
667	      printf 'SELECTOR UNAVAILABLE — every known recovery is listed, lowest privilege first:\n'
668	      printf 'RECOVERY A — no shell required. WRITE build-os/packets/routing/routing-request.json with {"task_id":"<id>","description":"<one line>","descriptor":{...13 fields...}}, then retry.\n'
669	      printf 'RECOVERY B — via shell: build-os/tools/route-task.sh --task-id <id> --description "<one line>" --descriptor <13-field-json>\n'
670	      printf 'Continue the task — only this unrouted call is refused, not the work.\n'
671	      logrow "$tid" "-" "RECOVERY-FALLBACK" "tool=$tool reason=selector-unavailable"
672	    fi
673	    return 0
674	  fi
675	  # The fire-once REASSESS trip: armed by the counter, enforced here, reset by
676	  # a reassessment record (fresh receipt = fresh state file; or an escalation/
677	  # degradation entry landing after the arming snapshot).
678	  local sf armed esc_s deg_s snap_esc snap_deg
679	  sf="$SDIR/$(basename "$rec" .md).tsv"
680	  armed=""
681	  if [ -f "$sf" ]; then
682	    armed="$(awk -F'\t' '$2=="reassess_block"||$2=="reassess_reset"{a=""} $2=="reassess_armed"{a=$3} END{print a}' "$sf")"
683	  fi
684	  if [ -n "$armed" ]; then
685	    esc_s="-"; deg_s="-"
686	    v="$(fval "$rec" escalation_evidence)"; [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != "-" ] && esc_s="set"
687	    v="$(fval "$rec" degradation_note)";    [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != "-" ] && deg_s="set"
688	    snap_esc="$(printf '%s' "$armed" | sed -n 's/.*esc=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"; [ -n "$snap_esc" ] || snap_esc="-"
689	    snap_deg="$(printf '%s' "$armed" | sed -n 's/.*deg=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"; [ -n "$snap_deg" ] || snap_deg="-"
690	    if [ "$esc_s" != "$snap_esc" ] || [ "$deg_s" != "$snap_deg" ]; then
691	      staterow "$rec" reassess_reset "reason=reassessment-record-landed esc=$esc_s deg=$deg_s (armed snapshot esc=$snap_esc deg=$snap_deg)" || true
692	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "REASSESS-RESET" "tool=$tool $armed"
693	      # fall through to ALLOW — the trip is reset, the counters restart
694	    else
695	      staterow "$rec" reassess_block "$armed fired=once" || true
696	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "BLOCK-REASSESS" "tool=$tool $armed"
697	      printf 'BLOCK\n'
698	      printf 'routing-gate: MUTATION BLOCKED ONCE — REASSESS. A repetitive parent loop tripped on receipt %s (%s). Where the trip is the token proxy, its value is tier ESTIMATE — chars/4, never billing truth. The thresholds are derived defaults, operator-tunable (ROUTING_REASSESS_SAME_TOOL_MAX, ROUTING_REASSESS_PROXY_MULT). Re-route before continuing: confirm the mode via build-os/tools/route-task.sh (a fresh receipt), or record an evidence-bearing escalation on the receipt, or degrade honestly via build-os/tools/record-degradation.sh. This trip fires exactly once — the next mutation-capable call passes, and a reassessment record resets the trip. Continue the task — only this one call is refused, not the work.\n' "$(basename "$rec")" "$armed"
699	      return 0
700	    fi
701	  fi
702	  staterow "$rec" mutation_event "tool_name=$tool class=mutation" || return 1
703	  logrow "$tid" "$mode" "ALLOW-MUTATION" "tool=$tool"
704	  printf 'ALLOW\n'
705	  return 0
706	}

729	  printf 'selected_mode: %s\n' "$(fval "$rec" selected_mode)"
730	  printf 'task_dispatches: %s (EXACT, derived from %s)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" task_dispatch)" "${sf#"$DATA_ROOT/"}"
731	  printf 'process_dispatches: %s (EXACT, attributed governance_process)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" process_dispatch)"
732	  printf 'tool_events: %s (EXACT, sessions where the gate is loaded)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" tool_event)"
733	  printf 'exploratory_events: %s (EXACT — the explore half of the explore/execute split)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" exploratory_event)"
734	  printf 'mutation_events: %s (EXACT — admitted mutation-capable calls)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" mutation_event)"
735	  if [ -f "$sf" ]; then
736	    printf 'token_proxy: %s (ESTIMATE — sum of tool-input chars / 4; never billing truth)\n' \
737	      "$(awk -F'\t' '$2=="tool_event" && match($3,/chars=[0-9]+/){s+=substr($3,RSTART+6,RLENGTH-6)+0} END{print int(s/4)}' "$sf")"
738	  else
739	    printf 'token_proxy: 0 (ESTIMATE — no state rows yet)\n'
740	  fi
741	  printf 'tool_failures: %s (EXACT only where PostToolUse exposes status)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" tool_failure)"
742	  issued="$(fval "$rec" issued_at)"
743	  if elapsed="$(( $(date -u +%s) - $(date -ud "$issued" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))" 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$issued" ]; then
744	    printf 'elapsed_s: %s (EXACT, derived at read time: issued_at %s vs now)\n' "$elapsed" "$issued"
745	  else
746	    printf 'elapsed_s: - (issued_at unreadable)\n'
747	  fi
748	  printf 'tokens: unavailable_live (close-time reconciliation via telemetry where headless)\n'
749	  printf 'cost_usd: unavailable_live (close-time reconciliation via telemetry where headless)\n'
750	  return 0
751	}
752	
753	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- wrapper ----
754	CMD="${1:-}"
755	case "$CMD" in
756	  gate|mutgate|count|post|status) ;;
757	  -h|--help|help) sed -n '2,70p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; exit 0 ;;
758	  *) printf 'routing-gate: unknown command "%s" — expected gate|mutgate|count|post|status\n' "${CMD:-}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
759	esac

762	
763	# ALWAYS drain stdin first (the DEFECT-0013 lesson: an undrained producer under
764	# pipefail is a race) — and never let a read failure become a blocked call.

766

768	  # OPERATOR-ONLY escape, refused-by-default posture: it exists, it is
769	  # documented in routing_contract_live.md, and it ALWAYS leaves a trace.
770	  logrow "-" "-" "DISABLED-BY-OPERATOR" "cmd=$CMD ROUTING_GATE_DISABLE=1"
771	  exit 0
772	fi
773	
774	case "$CMD" in
775	  count)
776	    count_tool "$IN" || logrow "-" "-" "FAIL-OPEN" "cmd=count internal error"
777	    exit 0 ;;
778	  post)
779	    post_tool "$IN" || logrow "-" "-" "FAIL-OPEN" "cmd=post internal error"
780	    exit 0 ;;
781	  gate|mutgate)

783	    # with stderr silenced (incidental tool noise must not pollute a refusal),
784	    # but logrow's unwritable-store fallback line must still escape — a trace
785	    # that dies inside the capture is no trace (PACKET-0055).
786	    exec 9>&2
787	    if [ "$CMD" = "gate" ]; then
788	      OUT="$(gate_decide "$IN" 2>/dev/null)"; RC=$?
789	    else
790	      OUT="$(mutgate_decide "$IN" 2>/dev/null)"; RC=$?
791	    fi

793	    if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ "$DECISION" = "ALLOW" ]; then
794	      exit 0

796	      printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | sed '1d' >&2
797	      exit 2
798	    else
799	      # FAIL OPEN: a broken gate must not brick every session. Logged, because
800	      # a silent fail-open is an invisible outage of the control plane.
801	      logrow "-" "-" "FAIL-OPEN" "cmd=$CMD rc=$RC decision=${DECISION:-none}"
802	      exit 0
803	    fi ;;
